page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with one marginal reference at the left at the start of the first paragraph. Running head at top centre, page number at top right. Gathering signature at the bottom right. No catchword.

main_text.p: passo 382. quamquam tamen qui hæc tempora sequuti sunt authores Græci, nec hominis, nec nominis, errorisve huius meminerit,siue quod illis ignota fuerit hæc hærefis, siue quod statim propter Synodum Palæstinam, in qua damna-ta fuerat, extincta inter eos perierit: siue deni-que, quod Græci scriptores liberi arbitrij vim ex philosophorum prophanorum doctrina ni-mium iam extollentes,& prædicantes hunc Pe-lagianorum errorem vel leuem vel nullum existi-mauerunt,qui tamen est teterrimus,&omnium Iustitiariorum,siue Operistarum hæreticorum, qui sequuti sunt,sons & scaturigo vere dici po-test. Itaque neque Theodoretus in libro De fa-bul.hæretic.neque Ioannes Damascenus,neque cuiuslibet rei compilator & rhapsodus Nice-phorus Callistus hos hereticos commemorant.

Latinis vero episcopis fuerunt notissimi, quos varie multumque vexarunt, vt ex scriptis Am-brosij De vocatione Gentium, Hieronymi ad-uersus Pelagianos, Augustini ipsius toto 7.To-mo facile apparebit. Isidorus vero etiam huius meminit.Fuit autem Pelagius huius tam impiæ blasphemiæ author, Monachus primum Ro-mæ,postea vero ad presbyterij dignitatem euec-tus,vt Augustinus in epistolis scribit,alij etiam ad episcopale culmen putant peruenisse. A pa-tria vero Britannia, quæ maritima Galliæ regio est (vbi olim Armoricæ ciuitates vocabantur) Brito cognominatus, vt a Pelagio Samosatensi episcopo, qui pius&orthodoxus fuit, & ante hunc sub Valente vixit, distinguereτur. de quo meminit Theodoretus libro 4. hist. capite 13.

page.notes: The first word of the page is a fragment, "quamquam", continuing from the previous page. The reference "passo 382." is printed at the left, level with the first line; it is treated as a marginal note. The word "distinguereτur" in the last paragraph: the final letter is printed as a Greek-looking tau and is likely the printed "retur"; it is uncertain, so it is marked here: distinguereτur[?]. A faint, mirrored show-through near the bottom left ("toridi") is not printed text on this page and was left out. Printing hyphens are kept as printed. The running head was copied as DE HAERESIBUS. (printed HAERESIBVS.) under the u/v rule.
